from_quote: the first to be called the general assembly, and is to be chosen by the people of the respective States
rationale: Describing the first branch of the legislature, the paragraph names its choice "by the people of the respective States", the provision of Article I, Section 2, clause 1.
to_quote: chosen every second Year by the People of the several States

from_quote: in proportion to the number of their inhabitants, and is to consist of sixty-five members, with powers in the legislature to increase the number, not to exceed one for every thirty thousand inhabitants
rationale: The paragraph names the apportionment of the first branch by numbers, its first sixty-five members, and the limit of "one for every thirty thousand", all set in Article I, Section 2, clause 3.
to_quote: The Number of Representatives shall not exceed one for every thirty Thousand

from_quote: The second branch is to be called the senate, and is to consist of twenty-six members, two of which are to be chosen by the legislatures of each of the States.
rationale: The paragraph names the composition of the senate, two members "chosen by the legislatures of each of the States", set in Article I, Section 3, clause 1.
to_quote: two Senators from each State, chosen by the Legislature thereof

from_quote: representatives and direct taxes shall be apportioned among the several States, which may be included in this Union, according to their respective numbers, which shall be determined by adding to the whole number of free persons, including those bound to service for a term of years, and excluding Indians not taxed, three-fifths of all other persons.
rationale: Introduced as "The words are", the paragraph quotes in quotation marks the first sentence of Article I, Section 2, clause 3 ("in this Union" for "within this Union").
to_quote: Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States which may be included within this Union, according to their respective Numbers, which shall be determined by adding to the whole Number of free Persons, including those bound to Service for a Term of Years, and excluding Indians not taxed, three fifths of all other Persons.

from_quote: in the above recited clause, by the words, " all other persons.
rationale: The paragraph refers to "the above recited clause", quoted in the previous paragraph, and quotes its words "all other persons".

from_quote: these States are to be permitted to continue the inhuman traffic of importing slaves until the year 1808
rationale: The paragraph names the permission for States to continue importing slaves "until the year 1808", the year named in Article I, Section 9, clause 1.
to_quote: prior to the Year one thousand eight hundred and eight

from_quote: Delaware should have a representation in the senate equal to Massachusetts or Virginia
rationale: The paragraph names the equal representation of the States in the senate ("This article of the Constitution"), set in Article I, Section 3, clause 1.

from_quote: It will consist at first, of sixty-five, and can never exceed one for every thirty thousand inhabitants.
rationale: The paragraph names the first number of the house (sixty-five), the limit of "one for every thirty thousand", and New York's six members "on the present apportionment", all set in Article I, Section 2, clause 3.
to_quote: shall not exceed one for every thirty Thousand

from_quote: A majority of these, that is, thirty-three, are a quorum
rationale: The paragraph names the quorum of each house as a majority of its members, the rule in Article I, Section 5, clause 1.
to_quote: a Majority of each shall constitute a Quorum to do Business
